Huma Finance Pool Ecosystem Overview 🧵

A simple breakdown of how PayFi credit pools work, who’s involved, and why it matters. Stay with this.

1. What are Huma pools?

Each pool connects stablecoins to real-world payment tasks. 
Borrowers like fintechs then, access undercollateralized credit.
While lenders earn real yield from actual cash flows.

2. The core PayFi players

Right now, four key partners are building on Huma:

• Arf
• Jia
• Rain
• BSOS

3. Arf | Cross-border payments

8 active pools on Solana, Stellar and Scroll, facilitates same-day settlements for global money transmitters using USDC.

Around $197M in monthly originations

4. Jia | SME lending

Live on Celo and Polygon, it enables receivables-backed loans for small businesses in Kenya and the Philippines

Hence supporting underserved markets.

5. Rain | Web3-native credit cards

This runs on Celo, and provides credit lines to DAOs and Web3 startups
Stablecoin-backed cards with no traditional banks involved

6. BSOS | Green trade finance

Built on Polygon and targets supply chain finance for electric vehicles and green energy in Taiwan. Also leverages ERP systems to validate invoices onchain

7. Why this is important

With no speculation, no wrapped tokens, the huma pools settle real payments backed by stablecoins. The risk is programmable and yield is made transparent

8. What’s ahead

Having permissionless pools launching on Solana, users will choose borrowers, customize risk, and earn Feathers through Classic or Maxi Mode.

This way, onchain credit becomes open and direct

9. TL: DR

With 12 active pools, over $100M originated, real-world use cases already in motion. Also running on Solana, Celo, Polygon and Scroll.

Backed by stablecoins and built for global tells that PayFi is no longer a concept as @humafinance is making it work live, onchain, and at scale.

And it’s just getting started 💯

gHuma 🫡

Ps: pay no serious attention to the data on the visual as it is AI crafted and doesn't display accurate info.👇

MAULAN PA RIN PO! 🌧️

PAGASA raised an Orange Rainfall Warning over Zambales, Bataan and Pampanga as of 2 p.m. Tuesday due to continued heavy rains from the southwest monsoon.

The alert warns of threatening floods, especially in low-lying and flood-prone areas.

A Yellow Warning remains in effect for Metro Manila, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, Laguna and Tarlac, where flooding is possible if rains persist.

Light to moderate rains with occasional heavy downpours are also affecting Nueva Ecija and Quezon, according to PAGASA.

Hindi na rin tayo magtataka kung lahat noong mga nangyayari ay sasabihin nila na kaparte 'yan ng war on drugs at kasalanan 'yan ni president Duterte," pahayag ng bise.
